title:
Less ticket bouncing.
A clearer path to resolution.
narration: TicketPilot classifies support issues, recommends the right team, and finds relevant fixes from resolved tickets. Follow one request, from a blocked employee to a confirmed outcome.

title: Describe the problem once.
label: EMPLOYEE PORTAL
detail: Maya describes the issue in her own words.
narration: Meet Maya, a sales employee who cannot open her dashboard before a customer meeting. In Northstar's employee portal, she describes the problem and submits a request. She does not need to know which support team owns it. Her request now has a reference: I N C, twenty forty-eight.

title: TicketPilot classifies the issue.
label: AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION
detail: TicketPilot identifies the team from matching resolutions.
narration: TicketPilot classifies Maya's issue and recommends Applications, using similar resolved tickets. Daniel, the support engineer, receives that classification with matching cases and a suggested fix. He reviews the evidence before approving the route, and can override it when needed.

title: Inspect the evidence.
label: OPEN A MATCHING CASE
detail: The earlier case moved from Security to Applications.
narration: Daniel opens a matching case. Here, the request first went to Security, but Applications resolved it. The notes describe restoring the reporting role mapping. That is the evidence behind the suggestion. Daniel can inspect the source before deciding whether it applies to Maya's issue.

title: Approve the proposed route.
label: ROUTING APPROVAL
narration: TicketPilot has classified the issue. Daniel approves its proposed route to Applications. He can override that route if needed. The classification is already done.

title: Bring the fix into the workflow.
label: SUGGESTED FIX + SOURCE
detail: Then verify dashboard access. Source: KB-002.
narration: The suggested fix brings the relevant steps and a knowledge reference into the same workspace. Daniel reviews the instructions, records the work, and sends Maya an update. The access change is simulated in this portfolio demo. In a real deployment, an authorized team would perform and verify that work.

title: Close the loop with Maya.
label: EMPLOYEE CONFIRMATION
detail: Maya checks her dashboard before confirming.
takeaway: Still broken? Ask for more help
narration: Maya returns to the same request. She can see what support did and what to check next. She opens her dashboard, verifies access, and selects Confirm it works. If the issue remains, she can select Still need help. Closing a ticket is only useful when the employee's problem is actually solved.

title: Give managers a view of service health.
label: SERVICE LEADER VIEW
detail: Elena reviews workload, transfers and human decisions.
takeaway: Validate the value in a pilot
narration: Meet Elena, the IT service manager. She sees Maya's closed request alongside service health and how engineers handled TicketPilot's recommendations. The goal is fewer avoidable transfers and less repeated investigation. These dashboard numbers are sample data. A pilot must measure actual handoffs, resolution time, and employee outcomes.

title: A clearer path, from request to outcome.
narration: For employees, one request to track. For support, an owner recommendation and a relevant fix with sources. For leaders, visibility into service outcomes. That is the value proposition to validate in a pilot.
